title: Spot Delivery on Vehicle Purchase Agreements
content:
**F&I guidance — spot delivery, Vehicle Purchase Agreements.**

- **Availability.** Spot delivery is offered only where the deal type allows spot delivery. It is available only on a deal financed by a dealer-arranged installment contract, as the deal's financing record shows.
- **Becoming final.** The delivery becomes final only if a lender approves the contract as written within the deal type's lender approval window, in calendar days after the delivery date.
- **Unwind timing.** A spot-delivered deal is unwound only when the handling date is later than the delivery date plus the approval window without lender approval. Calendar days are added to the delivery date, which is day 0. The lender has the whole last day, so an unwind is possible from the next calendar day.
- **On an unwind.** Every deposit and payment the buyer made is returned in full, every charge is reversed, and the trade-in vehicle is handed back. Miles driven during the spot delivery are not charged, because no deal type allows that charge.
- **New terms.** A buyer who prefers to sign a new contract on terms a lender has approved does so as a new deal. The unwound deal is not rewritten.

## Timing check (hypothetical: a 10-day approval window, delivery on the 8th of a month, no lender approval)

| Handling date | Unwind possible |
|---|---|
| the 18th (delivery plus 10) | no: the lender still has this whole day |
| the 19th | yes |

| Financing on the deal | Spot delivery |
|---|---|
| dealer-arranged installment contract | available where the deal type allows it |
| cash, outside lender or fleet net terms | not available |
